content.value_statement: Startup teams often need a complete business case before investors or partners can evaluate the opportunity. This skill structures the document, prompts for missing inputs, and turns strategy data into investor-ready sections.
actual_capabilities: Collects company stage, audience, target customer, problem, traction, and available materials before drafting.
Structures a business case with executive summary, market, product, competition, financials, team, risks, and funding sections.
Provides templates for financial snapshots, competitive matrices, metrics, hiring plans, and use of proceeds.
Suggests optional sections for regulated markets, deep technology, biotechnology, unit economics, and partnerships.
Creates a one-page executive summary slide outline for investor review.
Offers Markdown filename guidance and presentation preparation tips.
limitations: It relies on user-provided metrics, assumptions, and source material for accuracy.
It does not guarantee investor interest, valuation, or fundraising results.
It drafts business-case content but does not build spreadsheet models by itself.
PDF conversion and final visual design require separate tools or manual work.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Fundraising Business Case
use_cases.description: Build a complete business case for seed, Series A, or strategic investor conversations.

use_cases.title: Audit a Startup Strategy Narrative
use_cases.description: Check whether market size, positioning, financial logic, and risk sections support the investment story.

use_cases.title: Create an Internal Planning Document
use_cases.description: Turn product, market, hiring, and financial assumptions into a shared planning document for leadership.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Basic Business Case
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a founder with limited materials.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a startup business case for [company]. Ask me for any missing basics before drafting the first outline.

prompt_templates.title: Draft for Investor Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for a fundraising document.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an investor-ready business case for [company] targeting [investor type]. Include market, solution, traction, financials, team, risks, and funding ask.

prompt_templates.title: Refine Existing Materials
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for teams with a pitch deck or notes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my existing notes to create a business case. Identify gaps, weak assumptions, unsupported claims, and sections needing better data.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Board-Level Case
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for detailed strategic planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a board-level business case with base, conservative, and optimistic assumptions. Include go-to-market strategy, unit economics, hiring plan, risks, and milestone-based funding use.

output_examples.input: A seed-stage SaaS company needs a document for angel investors.
output: Executive summary with company overview, problem, solution, traction, and funding ask.
Market opportunity section with TAM, SAM, SOM, customer profile, and source notes.
Financial and use-of-proceeds sections with assumptions, milestones, and risk mitigations.

output_examples.input: A founder has a pitch deck and wants to find missing business-case sections.
output: Gap review covering competition, unit economics, hiring plan, and regulatory risk.
Recommended additions for investor diligence and internal alignment.
Priority list for data that should be verified before sharing the document.

output_examples.input: A product team needs an internal case for a new market expansion.
output: Market and customer analysis for the expansion opportunity.
Go-to-market plan with channels, pricing, sales motion, and success metrics.
Scenario-based financial summary with milestones and execution risks.

best_practices: Provide real metrics, data sources, and current traction before requesting the final draft.
State the target reader and decision goal so the document uses the right emphasis.
Review every financial and market assumption before sharing the business case externally.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for investor-ready claims without evidence or source material.
Do not treat generated projections as validated financial advice.
Do not use the same business case for every investor or partner audience.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a structured startup business case with market, product, financial, team, risk, and funding sections.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: Founders, advisors, and business teams can use it for fundraising, partnerships, or internal planning.

faq.question: Does it replace a financial model?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes financial assumptions and projections, but a spreadsheet model should validate the numbers.

faq.question: Can it use existing pitch materials?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide decks, notes, market research, or financial assumptions so it can build a stronger document.

faq.question: Does it verify market data?
faq.answer: It can organize and cite provided sources, but users should verify market data before external use.

faq.question: What output format does it target?
faq.answer: The visible instructions target a Markdown business case and suggest later conversion to PDF for sharing.
